name: Walt Whitman
bio: American poet, author of Leaves of Grass (first published 1855; its 1882 eighth edition was withdrawn by its publishers on a threatened prosecution for indecency). By 1882 he was living in Camden, New Jersey, across the Delaware from Philadelphia, partly paralysed since 1873. During the American lecture tour of 1882 Wilde visited him there twice - on 18 January, taken by the Philadelphia publisher J. M. Stoddart at Whitman's written invitation, and again in early May - and Wilde's one surviving letter to him (postmarked 1 March 1882) relays Swinburne's admiration and declares an intent to visit again before leaving America. Whitman kept that letter until 1888, when he handed it to Horace Traubel, whose Camden conversation records preserve Whitman's side of the acquaintance.
bio_note: Dates (1819-92), Camden residence, the 18 January visit with Stoddart, and the Leaves of Grass withdrawal are from the biographical footnote at Holland & Hart-Davis, Complete Letters (2000), p. 144 n. 1 (repo PDF 167, printed folio confirmed). Letter postmark and closing from pp. 144-5 (repo PDF 167-168, same session). Second visit 'early in May' 1882: Ellmann, 'Oscar Meets Walt', NYRB 3 Dec. 1987 (read at article page). 1888 letter handover: Traubel, With Walt Whitman in Camden, vol. 2, pp. 287-8 (IA withwaltwhitmani0002unse_c4l4, IIIF page images).
